scope.subject: PostgreSQL 18 V001 database foundation and application/audit role boundary
scope.stage: implementation ready; runtime proof and protected merge pending
scope.mutation_class: G3-sensitive database/authentication/authorization foundation; isolated test-only runtime execution

risk.rationale: The migration creates persistent identity, role, rights, audit and outbox structures and changes database permissions. Production/identity hard override SAFE-005 applies. No unverified static result is used to lower the residual tier.
hard_overrides: SAFE-005 Production and Identity: no production DB execution or role provisioning in this run.
SAFE-002 Destructive Action: temporary test-volume cleanup is limited to the exact generated Compose project.
SAFE-010 Self-approval: CI/review/merge and T013 checkbox remain separate human gates.
unknowns: PostgreSQL 18 migration execution is pending because Docker Compose and psql are unavailable locally.
The production login role and membership provisioning are intentionally outside V001 and require a later deployment decision.
Spring/Flyway runtime wiring and worker behavior are future tasks, not T013 proof.

controls.note: Implementation, verification and merge/read-back are separate graph nodes; merge and checkbox require explicit human approval.
The patch is limited to V001, its PostgreSQL verification harness, CI wiring and T013 evidence; V002+ and runtime are excluded.
The migration stores OIDC issuer/subject and rights metadata only; fixtures use synthetic identifiers and no real user/media data.
No credentials, passwords, tokens or production connection values are present in the migration, script or evidence.
The exact SQL/privilege assertion harness is implemented; P2 execution in PostgreSQL 18 is still required before this control can reduce residual risk.
The coding-agent patch allowlist is explicit and the verification script uses one isolated Compose service/project with no production target.
Protected merge, task completion and any production role/migration action remain human gates.
The test is isolated, bounded, idempotency-aware and cleans only its exact temporary project/volume; production execution is not attempted.
The workflow stops and records a blocker when Docker/psql is absent rather than substituting H2 or a shared database.
audit_event ownership and app grants are explicit; the test asserts app append succeeds while UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE fail.
Production backup/restore and expand-contract rollback belong to T082; T013 only guarantees no production execution and disposable-test cleanup.
